parsed.elsewhere_quote: Conversely, if $S$ meets every member of $\mathcal F$, choose an integer $x\ge a_1$ with support $S$. Every accepted integer smaller than $x$ has support in $\mathcal F$, and thus is noncoprime to $x$. Hence the greedy scan accepts $x$, proving $S\in\mathcal F$.
parsed.explanation: The reverse implication in (2) silently uses upward closure: if $C\in\mathcal F$ and $C\subseteq S$, then $S\in\mathcal F$. The quoted passage does not say this. However, the fully proved self-duality (1) establishes it immediately: $C$ meets every member of $\mathcal F$, so its superset $S$ does too, and the displayed converse gives $S\in\mathcal F$. Thus the required characterization is established elsewhere; adding one sentence would remove the local omission.
